propositions: Write operations (transition/claim/create) are exposed through three adapters (Python lib, CLI, MCP) with hand-mirrored input surfaces, but parameters silently drift between adapters (e.g., reason/caused_by/force missing in MCP).

A mechanical conformance oracle using a shared transport-agnostic contract table executes behavioral test cases across all three adapters against fresh stores, flagging any divergence in ACCEPTED/REJECTED/PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED outcomes.

The contract covers force (str | None), reason, caused_by, ref, close_class—the sanctioned write-op surface—and deliberately excludes legacy force_close; runtime conditional rules (reason required for certain close classes, close_class required for bug closes) are asserted behaviorally.

Current MCP param gaps (reason/caused_by/force on transition and claim) are encoded as strict-xfail rows citing scratchy-leprous-galago; transition's coupled-force shape (introduced by blusterous-earthly-kitten) is strict-xfail citing that ticket, keeping the suite green in CI regardless of landing order.

The oracle reuses and extends the existing three-adapter harness (tests/interfaces/adapters.py: Outcome, Adapter protocol, LibraryAdapter/CliAdapter/McpAdapter) by threading force/reason/close_class/caused_by/ref parameters through each transport's transition/claim/create methods.
Adapter-bound internals (source, return_alias, _creation_channel, repo_root) are excluded from the contract so they do not register as false divergences.
